ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, with C as the common vertex, in $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle CED$, $\angle ACB=\angle CDE=90^\circ$ and $\angle A=\angle DCE=30^\circ$, and with point D on line segment $AB$, what is $\angle ABE$? If $AC=10$ and $CD=9$, what is the length of $BE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Given that $\angle ACB=\angle CDE=90^\circ$ and $\angle A=\angle DCE=30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle DBC=\angle DEC=60^\circ$,\\
hence, points B, C, D, and E are concyclic,\\
therefore $\angle DBE=\angle DCE=30^\circ$,\\
which leads us to conclude that $\angle ABE=\boxed{30^\circ}$,\\
considering that in right triangle $ABC$, $\tan\angle BAC=\frac{BC}{AC}$,\\
thus $BC=AC\cdot\tan30^\circ=10\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=\frac{10\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
similarly, in right triangle $CED$, $\cos\angle DCE=\frac{CD}{CE}$,\\
therefore $CE=\frac{CD}{\cos30^\circ}=\frac{9}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}=6\sqrt{3}$,\\
given $\angle ABC=60^\circ$ and $\angle ABE=30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle CBE=\angle ABC+\angle ABE=90^\circ$,\\
consequently, $BE=\sqrt{CE^2-BC^2}=\sqrt{108-\frac{300}{9}}=\boxed{\frac{4\sqrt{42}}{3}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, with C as the common vertex, in $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle CED$, $\angle ACB=\angle CDE=90^\circ$ and $\angle A=\angle DCE=30^\circ$, and with point D on line segment $AB$, what is $\angle ABE$? If $AC=10$ and $CD=9$, what is the length of $BE$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:}

Given that $\angle ACB=\angle CDE=90^\circ$ and $\angle A=\angle DCE=30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle DBC=\angle DEC=60^\circ$,\\
hence, points B, C, D, and E are concyclic,\\
therefore $\angle DBE=\angle DCE=30^\circ$,\\
which leads us to conclude that $\angle ABE=\boxed{30^\circ}$,\\
considering that in right triangle $ABC$, $\tan\angle BAC=\frac{BC}{AC}$,\\
thus $BC=AC\cdot\tan30^\circ=10\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=\frac{10\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
similarly, in right triangle $CED$, $\cos\angle DCE=\frac{CD}{CE}$,\\
therefore $CE=\frac{CD}{\cos30^\circ}=\frac{9}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}=6\sqrt{3}$,\\
given $\angle ABC=60^\circ$ and $\angle ABE=30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle CBE=\angle ABC+\angle ABE=90^\circ$,\\
consequently, $BE=\sqrt{CE^2-BC^2}=\sqrt{108-\frac{300}{9}}=\boxed{\frac{4\sqrt{42}}{3}}$.

Also from the given conditions ∠CDE=90° and ∠DCE=30°, so in △CED, ∠DEC=60°. Thus ∠DBC=∠DEC=60°, and these two angles subtend the same chord DC, therefore the four points B, C, D, and E are concyclic. After being concyclic, the inscribed angles subtending the same chord DE are equal, so ∠DBE=∠DCE=30°. Also because BA and BD are rays starting from B in the same direction, ∠ABE=∠DBE=30°.

Length calculation: In the right triangle ABC, tan∠BAC=BC/AC, so BC=AC·tan30°=10·√3/3=10√3/3. In the right triangle CED, cos∠DCE=CD/CE, so CE=CD/cos30°=9/(√3/2)=6√3.
